Brian A. Foster for CVUSD School Board Area #4
Vote November 3, 2026
# Academic Achievement is Priority #1
Brian A. Foster is running for CVUSD school board to provide greater Rigor, Respect, and Responsibility for students and teachers.
Education Priorities
## A clear agenda for stronger local schools
- Increased Rigor with honest grading
- Greater Respect for families, students, and teachers
- Matching student and teacher Responsibility with authority
These three R’s (Rigor, Respect, and Responsibility) reflect a straightforward commitment to higher expectations, student responsibility, and transparent school board leadership.
## Let’s Restore Castro Valley’s Academic Performance
From Average Back to Excellent!
We need an urgent change in leadership to focus on what matters the most: Academic Achievement!
While our school district proclaims that we have “Excellent” schools, the truth is that our academic performance is now just “Average.” Alameda County’s Academic Scorecard (CAASPP) results for ELA (English Language Arts) and Math graphically display the truth in the two graphics below. The table below the graphs shows only modest improvements from 2024-2025, with half of our high school students below proficiency in math and 30% below proficiency in English.
Castro Valley’s English scores indicate that students are 36.6 points above standard, which is roughly half-way within the standard range. The vertical yellow line shows the statewide average, which is -8.1 points (below standard). Castro Valley’s math scores indicate that students are 15.5 points above standard, which is not significantly above standard. The vertical yellow line shows the statewide average, which is -42.4 points (below standard). Castro Valley’s English and math scores have shown only modest improvement from 2024 to 2025. At CVHS, about 70% of our students are proficient or advanced in English (30% below grade level), but only 50% are proficient or advanced in math (50% below grade level).
## But Don’t We Have High Graduation Rates?
CVUSD is proud of its 96% high school graduation rate, which the district has maintained for two consecutive years. The district is not telling you that most school districts in Alameda County have graduation rates in the 90-100% range. We also know that the quality and meaning of a high school diploma varies significantly among districts. The graph below displays the official 2025 graduation rates for Alameda County schools reporting to the State of California:
Most school districts in Alameda County share Castro Valley’s high graduate rates, but we clearly have different levels of academic rigor. The gap between CVHS’s graduation rates and its English, math, and science scores shows how much a high school diploma has been devalued over time, and why colleges are now crying about how high school diplomas and high grade point averages (GPAs) have come to signify little more than middle school mastery.
Does anyone really believe that Castro Valley’s diploma represents greater academic accomplishment than Fremont’s? The value of a CVHS diploma can be gauged against its standardized test (CAASP) scores. In English, 67% of our students are proficient or better, meaning 33% are below standard. In math, 59% of our students are proficient or better, meaning 41% are below standard. In science, only 50% of our students are proficient or better, meaning half are below standard.
The question to ask is how is it possible that 33-50% of our students are below standard in core subjects, yet CVUSD still graduates them? The large gaps between graduation rates and proficiency levels indicate how grades and course credits do not reflect true academic accomplishment. Remember that the State of California rewards districts for high graduation rates: it does not consider how those graduation rates are achieved.
## Is Your Child Truly Ready for College-Level Work?
You’ve probably read the headlines from university professors in recent months decrying the decline of academic preparation of high school students being admitted to higher education. They cite a large percentage of incoming freshmen who are performing at the middle school level. Prior to COVID, the SAT/ACT tests screened out unprepared students, but many universities have not yet reinstated those tests. Until then, perhaps the best proxy measure to ensure your student is prepared for college is the Advanced Placement (AP) test. Click the button below to read a University of California, Berkeley professor’s cry for help.
I teach calculus at Berkeley. Some of my students can’t do middle school math—Zvezdelina Stankova
## Three R’s for Academic Achievement
### Rigor
Increase access to Advanced Placement classes so more students can take rigorous courses, challenge themselves, and prepare for college success. Eliminate the Equity grading requirement where students earn half credit for doing nothing.
### Respect
Set clear academic and behavioral standards, and then tell students and families the truth about their performance. Support teacher authority with the respect that adults deserve.
### Responsibility
Match student accountability with authority by reinforcing clear standards, supporting educators, and restoring a culture of responsibility in every classroom. Celebrate real academic success and address academic shortcomings as early as possible.

# Endorsements for
# Brian A. Foster
Brian A. Foster (left) supporting Alameda County Supervisor Nate Miley (center) and Matt Turner (right) distributing oranges at the Castro Valley Rowell Ranch Parade.
## Community Endorsements
I am pleased to endorse Brian A. Foster for the Castro Valley Unified School Board.
Mr. Foster taught social studies (history, government, and economics) at Newark Memorial High School for four years, and during that time he also encouraged students to participate in civic engagement, early voter registration, and volunteer projects.
I grew up in Castro Valley and have always appreciated its small town flavor, similar to Newark, and your town’s commitment to academic excellence.
Please vote for my good friend, Brian, who has a passion for ensuring a quality education for all students.
—Michael Hannon
Mayor, City of Newark, Raised in Castro Valley
I am proud to endorse Brian Foster for Castro Valley Unified School District Board Area 4.
Brian has demonstrated a strong commitment to our community, thoughtful leadership, and a genuine interest in ensuring that Castro Valley students receive the best possible educational opportunities. As a longtime resident, business owner, and community advocate, I believe our schools benefit from leaders who listen, engage with the community, and focus on practical solutions that support students, teachers, and families.
Brian brings the experience, integrity, and dedication needed to help guide our school district through future challenges and opportunities. I am confident he will serve the students and residents of Castro Valley with professionalism and a commitment to excellence.
—Ken Carbone
Castro Valley Resident, Business Owner & Community Advocate

## Video Endorsement from Mary Beth Tinker
Mary Beth Tinker from the Supreme Court case, Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District (1969), encourages Mr. Foster to continue teaching students about their rights and how to use them.
## What Mr. Foster’s Students and Parents Say
“We have been thinking about you so much and I miss your history class more than anything, to my favorite teacher, from your favorite student.”
—Albany High School Graduate
“To do this, she switched into Mr. Foster’s advisory class for the spring semester. It was an intense process since he had to cover the entire course in half the time. Mr. Foster went above and beyond in his efforts to help a student who clearly had a hunger to learn more. When you find teachers who love what they do and are good at it, it’s important to hang onto them for the sake of the students.”
—Albany High School Parent
“You are one of the only teachers that didn’t give up on me and didn’t push me aside, and it really means a lot.”
—Newark Memorial High School Graduate
“You’ve actually taught me more than any other academic teacher has. You’ve always cared about my well-being and respected me as a person and for that I gave you my respect as a student but also as just a young man growing up.”
—Newark Memorial High School Graduate
“You are absolutely amazing, don’t ever let anyone tell you otherwise. You are the true definition of what a teacher should be, a genuine educator, who prioritizes your students in every way they deserve. You are the best thing that can happen to any student who is fortunate enough to call you their teacher.”
—Newark Memorial High School Parent
“Mr. Foster, I just wanted to thank you so much for being my teacher this year. You have made me feel welcomed in your class the whole year. I will miss you a lot.”
—Newark Memorial High School Student (graduated U.C. Berkeley years ahead of schedule)
“Thank god I still have notes from your class Mr.Foster! It’s helping me with my Macroeconomic class!”
—Oakland Military Institute High School Student (using high school notes in his college class)
